author: EmuCore - Hub
title: PCSX2 reshapes AA1 line smoothing for high-resolution rendering
summary: A line-direction-aware expansion narrows the blur around upscaled AA1 geometry, targeting outlines that became too soft when the original GS behavior was magnified six times.
heroAlt: Visual evidence from PCSX2 pull request #14480: GS/HW: Adjust line AA1 blur with upscaling.

sourceLabels.pcsx2-pr-14480: GS/HW: Adjust line AA1 blur with upscaling.

blocks.text: Native AA1 width becomes excessive when every pixel is magnified

The PlayStation 2 GS expands antialiased line coverage along axis directions. At native resolution that behavior is part of the original rasterizer, but multiplying the internal resolution can turn its edge region into a visibly wide blur. Pull request #14480 treats this as an upscaling-quality problem: preserve smoothing around the line while reducing how much neighboring high-resolution image area it softens.
Perpendicular expansion follows the line instead of the screen axes

The revised shaders and common GS setup expand AA1 lines in the direction perpendicular to the segment. The blur width and transition region are reduced at the same time. Because the adjustment follows line geometry, a diagonal outline is no longer widened as if it were two independent horizontal and vertical edges. The change is intentionally aesthetic rather than a claim of exact GS rasterization at scaled resolutions.
The scope stops at AA1 lines

AA1 triangles are not changed, so games using antialiasing on triangle edges should retain the previous path. The article's evidence is instead the yellow lock-on box in Armored Core, character and interface outlines in Sly 2, and building lines in The Incredibles. Each comparison uses a six-times scale and includes AA1-disabled reference images, making it possible to separate the filter from the underlying artwork.
Review needs identical scenes and several line orientations

Testing should enable the AA1 option and capture the same frame at native resolution and multiple upscale factors. Straight, diagonal, thin, and intersecting lines need separate inspection because perpendicular expansion changes with direction. The reported game set is a useful baseline, but reviewers should also look for gaps, uneven thickness, excess shimmer, or outlines that become sharper than the non-AA1 reference rather than assuming less blur is always better.
The change deliberately favors cleaner high-resolution AA1 lines; it does not alter AA1 triangles or present the scaled result as an exact reproduction of native GS coverage.
